subject: HealthSpan BYOK / retention & audit logs — triage and next steps
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@healthspan.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: HealthSpan compliance questions: BYOK, retention windows, and audit exports

Hi Irene —

Thanks for taking this. We're starting an evaluation of Redwood for a production pilot and have a short compliance checklist we need answers for before the pilot kickoff. Quick bullets below — full questionnaire attached.

- Retention: we require configurable retention by tenant and an option for a 30/90/365 day policy; can we get per-tenant retention controls and a soft-delete window for 30 days?
- Audit logs: need per-request audit logs with user/session identifiers, exportable in NDJSON, and an archive path to our S3. Is export supported?
- BYOK / KMS: customer-managed keys preferred. Would Redwood allow BYOK + escrow for disaster recovery, or is a key-proxy/ephemeral approach required? What are limits?
- SSO: SCIM provisioning + SCIM deltas are mandatory for our enterprise SSO provider.

We have a tight timeline — pilot in 6 weeks. If you can summarize feasible options and high-level effort estimates, that will help triage with procurement.

Attached: HealthSpan_compliance_questionnaire.pdf

Appreciate the quick pairing here.

Best,
Anna Lopez
Head of Security Operations
HealthSpan Analytics
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@healthspan.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthSpan compliance questions: BYOK, retention windows, and audit exports

Thanks Anna — received and read. We'll run a quick triage across security, product, and infra and propose a pilot-safe approach that minimizes scope for the initial 6-week run.

High-level options we expect to propose (short):
1) BYOK with limited escrow: customer brings a KMS key in their cloud account + optional escrow key held in a sealed HSM for catastrophic recovery. Pros: meets BYOK requirement; Cons: longer onboarding (KMS handshake, policy alignment).
2) Ephemeral key-proxy (short-lived keys): faster onboarding, no escrow, short retention for KV/cache but requires clear deletion proofs and enhanced logging.
3) Hybrid: BYOK for customer storage blobs + ephemeral keys for session-level inference.

Open questions for HealthSpan (Anna):
- Do you need full-model request traces in the audit export, or is metadata (request id, timestamp, caller id, route, model version) sufficient for this pilot?
- Is the S3 export path reachable from a dedicated VPC endpoint or will we need signed upload tokens?

I've attached a quick triage matrix (triage-matrix-20270308.csv) with suggested owners, estimated effort (S/M/L), and blocking risks.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Security (Jonas) to confirm minimum audit log fields and retention carveouts.
- Product (Marissa) to weigh in on acceptable rollback/QA gating for a BYOK onboarding flow.
- Infra/Eng to estimate calendar days for KMS handshake + SCIM provisioning (I'll loop infra once we choose path).

I'll schedule a 30m triage tomorrow to align — does 11:00 PT work for everyone?

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Senior Compliance PM
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Anna Lopez <anna@healthspan.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthSpan compliance questions: BYOK, retention windows, and audit exports

Irene / Anna — quick tech note from Security:

- Minimum audit fields for pilot: timestamp, request_id, model_id, route, caller_id (tenant+user), response_status, token_length, and key_id if BYOK used. We should also include the KMS key fingerprint where possible.
- For export to customer S3: prefer signed PUTs via a short-lived presigned URL from Redwood; direct cross-account role assumption (sts:AssumeRole) is doable but requires legal + infra sign-off (longer).
- BYOK escrow: I'm cautious. Escrowed keys add attack surface — if we provide an escrow option, it must be sealed in an HSM with documented access logs and quarterly access reviews. That increases program overhead.
- Retention carveouts: allow a short-term soft delete (30d) for operational recovery, then hard purge. Need indexing to support partial restores for 90d window if requested (S medium).

Blocking items:
- Legal approval for cross-account key escrow (if requested) — estimated 3–4 weeks.
- Engineering risk: we need a safe path for key rotation without downtime; schedule depends on infra bandwidth.

I'll join the 11:00 PT triage.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna@healthspan.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthSpan compliance questions: BYOK, retention windows, and audit exports

Thanks — quick product checklist/questions from my side before the triage:

1) Scope: for the pilot, are we comfortable with metadata-only audit exports (no full prompt content)? That materially reduces risk and dev effort. Anna — please confirm if metadata suffices for initial pilot.
2) Rollout model for BYOK: recommend a phased approach — (A) pilot with ephemeral key-proxy + S3 export, (B) BYOK for blobs only, (C) full BYOK handshake for token encryption. Each phase gated by QA and a small tenant list.
3) SCIM: we can support basic SCIM provisioning quickly; delta sync (SCIM bulk changes) will be a separate sprint.

If Anna is ok with metadata-only exports and the phased rollout, we can commit to a 6-week pilot with milestones: week 1 onboarding + SCIM smoke, week 2 KMS handshake (if chosen) / otherwise key-proxy work, week 3 audit export proof-of-concept, week 4 pilot run + smoke, weeks 5–6 iterate and prepare docs.

I'll have a draft mutual action plan in Drive by EOD: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3C-triage-plan

Marissa
Senior PM, Product Security
Redwood Inference
From: Anna Lopez <anna@healthspan.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Michael Trent <michael.trent@healthspan.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HealthSpan compliance questions: BYOK, retention windows, and audit exports

Thanks, everyone — this is helpful. Confirming:

- For pilot we accept metadata-only audit exports (no content). That speeds things up.
- We prefer the phased rollout Marissa outlined. We'll take ephemeral key-proxy for pilot and target BYOK blobs in phase 2.
- S3 export via presigned URLs is acceptable. We'll provide a bucket and a dev role for the pilot.

Michael (cc'd) will send the bucket details and legal contact for minimal MSA edits. We'll also sign the mutual NDA already in DocuSign (link below) before kickoff.

Anna
